description_full: easyJet plc operates as a low-cost airline carrier in Europe. The company engages in the development of building projects; financing and insurance business; and tour operator activities, as well as provides holiday packages. It also offers heavy base maintenance and air transport services. easyJet plc was founded in 1995 and is headquartered in Luton, the United Kingdom.
ceo_bio: Mr. Alistair Kenton Jarvis | CEO, Member of the Management Board & Director | Age 57 | Compensation: $2.4M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 19K people. Revenue per employee of $694K ranks in the top quartile among Industrials peers. Each employee generates $43K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $3K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 3× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity).
financial_summary: easyJet Plc is a mid-cap industrials business with a $6.8B market cap on $13.3B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +21% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +2.5pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at 14% against a 8% cost of capital, a 7-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, and 17% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $824M in free cash flow — roughly 6 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.29× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 4.5×.
Shareholder yield is only 1.1%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 46% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 2% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 44% and a beta of 1.10, it moves roughly with the market.
Trading is thin (about $65K a day), below the $1.0M liquidity floor flagged; building a position would move the price.

val: The stock trades 72% below its DCF fair value of $32.06, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 58%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $24.67 to $42.76 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Industrials peers: P/E 12.4 vs 24.1, EV/EBITDA 7.7 vs 13.4 and P/FCF 8.2 vs 22.9 (sector median).
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 12.2% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 14.6% (vs the 8% bar).
The Street target $6.18 on average, 32% below the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 17.5% annual cash-flow growth, 27pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 14% earns above the cost of capital of 7.8%, but the 7pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.75).
It runs a 17% gross margin and converts 6% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 9/9 and cash conversion of 3.29x.
ROE of 14% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (3.3x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $795.2M.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 1.64 in the distress zone.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 21.4% over 3 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 14.4% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.0%), and institutions hold 0%.
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.1% (2.0% in dividends, less 0.9% of net share issuance).
people: With about 19,224 employees, each generates about $694K of revenue, 1.9x the Industrials median.
That works out to $43K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.4M (3x revenue per employee).
